I remember years ago, Red explained how to scan correlations.

As he said it, I marveled at its genius, and wondered how he could ever
have worked it out, so I asked. He answered "it just came to me".

Well, I forgot the wording of it quickly, and thought I'd never know again.

Some time later, I was checking a chart. Price had come to a level. So I
 went to another chart, and another, and another, knowing instinctively
where to go and what to look for.

The method came to me.

Everything becomes common sense to us in the end, no matter how rare that sense really is

author: ViTaLDRuG
text:
I guess everyone is getting ready for the new year :)

I have small question. When you have time, let me know your thoughts.

We usually mark our UFL/LFLs when price breaks a important level to the
left and then price its target. But sometimes price bounces at these FLs
 when it comes back to them or sometimes breaks FLs ignoring them. So we
 do not know exactly what FLs are with an importance which holds price
until price actually bounce at such FLs. May be we can guess the
important ones by looking at the approach.

Is it safe to consider a kink which hold a price up or down as a FL
without considering the levels it broke to the left(given that it hits
the target) I have shown these two cases below.

Image 1. shows where we consider a High(X) as an important level.
Breaking that and hitting the top HTF red FL will make the FL1. Then we
follow breaking of that FL and mark the FLs to the right and so on.

Image 2 shoes where we simply mark a kink(FL1) which held price up,
which hits target(Red HTF FL), then breaking these FL will create the
other FLs to the right. If we follow these two approaches, we will not
end up with the same set of FLs.

Another question is that, What is the important level in the first image
 X or what X is reacting to? So based on that, the FL1 in the first
image will be a different one too.

author: Astrokillah
text:
EURUSD

PinkPanther, Ysbail, dkd11, I am taking the risk of being accused of 'curve-fitting'.
 There is a saying that hindsight is always perfect, and if you look
hard enough, you will always find the exact reason that causes price to
turn.

I start with this visible swing low on H4, see point 1 on chart below:

you may argue that 1 is a reaction to FL-A, but most traders who doesn't
 understand FL would look at 1 and think that's a support and therefore
place buy orders there, therefore to break this swing low, it would
still require a significantly large sell order. That's why I went
searching for the FL that broke this swing low.

In chart below, I found the FL-B that broke below the swing low from
point 1. But I have also found several interesting elements:

I saw a smaller FL-C which breaks into the CPAZ, so this can be an important FL.

Then I saw a DP (green box) which delineated the upper edge of FL-B, and
 from my observations so far, in order to confirm PA to the north, we
need price to engulf not only FL-B, but also the DP that defined the
edge of it. If you think about it, even though we call FL-B a flag
limit, but on smaller scale it's actually a flag, and then the DP became
 the flag limit of Flag-B!.

Then I also saw a QM level inside FL-B, and I want to see what was responsible for breaking this QM level too.

Fast forward to 14 November 2017, where all of these elements were broken.

I see FL-C being engulfed by FL-D

QM-level being engulfed by FL-E

DP being engulfed by FL-F

So we now see how price reacting to each of these FLs.

Chart below showed price reacting to the upper edge of FL-F and bounced upwards

Then on 19 November, price plunged into FL-E and bounced upwards strongly

Then on 21 November, price hit FL-D twice, and the second time it 'almost' engulfed it.
